title: Composition isomorphisms transport a commuting square
statement: In any category let r1:A≅B, r2:C≅D, e:A≅C, s1:A′≅B′, s2:C′≅D′, e′:A′≅C′. Given a0:A→A′, a1:C→C′, b1:B→B′ and b2:D→D′ satisfying r1.hom;b1=a0;s1.hom, r2.hom;b2=a1;s2.hom and e.hom;a1=a0;e′.hom, then (r1.inv;e.hom;r2.hom);b2=b1;(s1.inv;e′.hom;s2.hom).

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(3), Proposition 6.8.11(3), Remark 6.8.15; explicit formal coefficient and adjunction argument

proof.text: Cancel the epimorphism r1.hom. Rewrite the two composition equations and the middle transport equation. Associativity and cancellation of s1 with its inverse finish.

theorem composition_square_aux {D : Type*} [Category D]
    {A B C D₀ A' B' C' D' : D}
    (r₁ : A ≅ B) (r₂ : C ≅ D₀) (e : A ≅ C)
    (s₁ : A' ≅ B') (s₂ : C' ≅ D') (e' : A' ≅ C')
    (a₀ : A ⟶ A') (a₁ : C ⟶ C') (β₁ : B ⟶ B') (β₂ : D₀ ⟶ D')
    (h₁ : r₁.hom ≫ β₁ = a₀ ≫ s₁.hom)
    (h₂ : r₂.hom ≫ β₂ = a₁ ≫ s₂.hom)
    (he : e.hom ≫ a₁ = a₀ ≫ e'.hom) :
    (r₁.inv ≫ e.hom ≫ r₂.hom) ≫ β₂ =
      β₁ ≫ (s₁.inv ≫ e'.hom ≫ s₂.hom)
